summary: U.S. equities pulled back Wednesday from record highs as rising oil prices and Treasury yields stoked inflation concerns ahead of the Fed's September FOMC minutes. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq closed at all-time highs Tuesday, but opened down 0.3% to 0.7% Wednesday as Brent crude climbed above $102 on Iranian attacks in the Strait of Hormuz and the 10-year Treasury yield approached 5.33%, its highest level since 2002. Crypto markets tumbled in sympathy, with Bitcoin falling below $84,000 and over $487 million in long positions liquidated within one hour. Traders are bracing for hawkish language in the FOMC minutes due at 2 p.m. ET, even though market pricing for an October rate hike has fallen to roughly 20% after a weak September jobs report. In company news, Constellation Energy and Vistra surged on multi-billion-dollar nuclear power deals with Alphabet and the Department of Energy, respectively, while Webull plunged 20% on reports of ties to China's government.

signals.title: Oil Spike and Treasury Yield Surge Hit Risk Assets
signals.desc: Brent crude broke $102 amid Iranian tanker attacks, pushing the 10-year Treasury yield to 24-year highs near 5.33% and triggering inflation fears that sent equities and crypto sharply lower.

signals.title: Crypto Liquidation Wave: $487M in Longs Wiped Out
signals.desc: Bitcoin dropped below $84,000 and Ethereum fell 5.8% as over $487 million in leveraged long positions liquidated in one hour, with crypto market cap down 3.8% to $2.925 trillion.

signals.title: Fed Minutes Expected to Show Hawkish Debate Despite Market Dovishness
signals.desc: September FOMC minutes (2 p.m. ET) will cover the unanimous 25bp rate hike decision, but market pricing for October hike has since plunged to 20% after weak jobs data, creating potential for volatility if tone is hawkish.

signals.title: Nuclear Power Deals Lift Constellation Energy +12.3%, Vistra +10.8%
signals.desc: Alphabet signed a $4.3 billion, 20-year nuclear power purchase agreement with Constellation Energy, while the DOE committed $4.2 billion to Vistra for facility upgrades, driving major rallies in both stocks.

signals.title: China Ties Report Sinks Webull 20%
signals.desc: Webull stock plunged 20% after U.S. lawmakers reportedly flagged that the trading platform is tied to China's government in structural ways, raising regulatory risk.

verdict: Markets face a cautious session as macro crosswinds intensify: oil-driven inflation fears and elevated Treasury yields pressure risk assets, while FOMC minutes at 2 p.m. ET could amplify volatility if the tone clashes with dovish market pricing.
